subject: A doubt regarding the mirt model

messages.subject: A doubt regarding the mirt model
parts:
Hello Phil,

Suppose we have two scenarios

Scenario 1:

items are located into specific factors  and  there are correlation among the factors. However it is not that factor X  is affecting the  items in factor Y or Z  directly.  The correlation  among the factors is not playing any role here.  In such situation is I think  we can use one-dimensional IRT models.  Since each sub subjects are affected  by  a single factor. So cross loadings will be zero.



Scenario 2:
 Here the factors  are correlated  and all  the factors have direct effect  on all the items. This is a more general  case. Which means all the items will have both  main loading and cross loadings.

For the scenario 2, following model will be 

## All the items are loaded into all the factors

## There will be correlation among the factors

cmodel <- mirt.model(
  ' F1 = x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3,z1,z2,z3
    F2 = x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3,z1,z2,z3
    F3 = x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3,z1,z2,z3
   COV = F1*F2*F3 '

)
mirt(data, cmodel)


 Above model is justifiable for the scenario 2?


Thanking you,
Irshad

On Fri, Oct 17, 2014 at 8:44 AM, Irshad Mujawar <irshadmuj...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello Phil,

Suppose we have two scenarios

Scenario 1:

items are located into specific factors  and  there are correlation among the factors. However it is not that factor X  is affecting the  items in factor Y or Z  directly.  The correlation  among the factors is not playing any role here.  In such situation is I think  we can use one-dimensional IRT models.  Since each sub subjects are affected  by  a single factor. So cross loadings will be zero.

You could treat these independent factors as unidimensional. The correlations between the factors give information about other factors, so factor scores will be more precise if you include all three factors at once (this is actually one reason to prefer an MCAT versus multiple CAT applications). Think of it this way, if factor 1 is about 'addition', factor 2 is about 'subtraction', and factor 1 and 2 correlate highly, then if you know that an individual is good at addition there is a very good chance they are also good at subtraction; including multiple dimensions allows for this idea statistically.

Scenario 2:
 Here the factors  are correlated  and all  the factors have direct effect  on all the items. This is a more general  case. Which means all the items will have both  main loading and cross loadings.

For the scenario 2, following model will be 

## All the items are loaded into all the factors

## There will be correlation among the factors

cmodel <- mirt.model(
  ' F1 = x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3,z1,z2,z3
    F2 = x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3,z1,z2,z3
    F3 = x1,x2,x3,y1,y2,y3,z1,z2,z3
   COV = F1*F2*F3 '

)
mirt(data, cmodel)


 Above model is justifiable for the scenario 2?

This model is incredibly weak, complicated, and not even identified. You'd be better off thinking about whether there is a bifactor structure than trying something like this. Cheers.

Phil 



Thanking you,
Irshad

On Mon, Oct 20, 2014 at 12:11 AM, Irshad Mujawar <irshadmuj...@gmail.com> wrote:
Many thanks for the reply.

Phil, I totally agree with you, in regards with this model may be week, complicated; but I did not get what do you mean by its not identified. Will you please say it in different set of words.

There is an infinite number of parameters that will fit this model equally well, since mathematically it is not uniquely solvable. The problem comes up a lot in SEM, so checking out literature there will help (http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/identifi.html). Your model is essentially an exploratory factor analysis model with 3 extra correlations being estimated in the latent variables, which is not possible since in order to identify a EFA the factors must be independent/orthogonal.

I just want to know whether my way of specification is correct for multidimensional data(in this case, data containing three factors).

Am I at least correct in the way I specified the model for the given scenario?

Yes, they sounded fine.

Phil
